status_summary: The two-site plutonium pit approach has continued: NNSA published a notice of intent for a programmatic environmental impact statement covering Los Alamos and Savannah River on 2025-05-09, and the draft became available on 2026-04-17, with comments open to 2026-07-16 and a final statement planned for early 2027. Public Law 119-21 (2025-07-04) provided 2 billion dollars for the nuclear sea-launched cruise missile and 400 million dollars for its warhead, per CRS, which also notes statutory deployment dates of 2032 and 2034. Trade press reported on 2026-01-29 that Los Alamos exceeded its pit production objectives and is working toward 30 pits per year by 2028, and Arms Control Today reported in September 2026 that construction of the Savannah River facility remains at an early stage, with completion expected between late 2031 and mid-2035. The stage is implemented because the funding, continued warhead development and two-site posture the text asks for are in effect, while quantity production is years away and no action on the B83 retirement was found.

timeline.event: NNSA published a notice of intent to prepare a programmatic environmental impact statement for plutonium pit production, with single-site and multi-site alternatives at Los Alamos and Savannah River.
Public Law 119-21 enacted; per CRS it includes 2 billion dollars for the nuclear sea-launched cruise missile and 400 million dollars to accelerate its warhead.
Trade press reported the Los Alamos director saying the lab exceeded its pit production objectives, with a working target of 30 pits per year by 2028.
EPA published the notice of availability of the draft pit production programmatic environmental impact statement, opening a 90-day comment period to 2026-07-16, with public hearings in May 2026.

Arms Control Today reported that construction of the Savannah River pit facility remains at an early stage with completion expected between late 2031 and mid-2035, that the plan of 30 pits a year at Los Alamos and 50 at Savannah River is still being executed, and that the FY2026 energy and water appropriations act directed NNSA to provide an internal review of its pit plans.

title: Fund new warheads, keep two plutonium pit sites, revive sea-launched cruise missile
uncertainties: Pit counts are classified, so progress rests on official statements relayed by trade press. The DOE hearing presentation (energy.gov) says a court settlement requires a record of decision on a set schedule; that litigation was not traced. A search for any decision to keep the B83 found nothing conclusive. A Center for Arms Control summary (armscontrolcenter.org, 2025-12-12) of the FY2026 NDAA conference text describes codification of the two-site plan of 30 pits at Los Alamos and 50 at Savannah River, 210 million dollars for the cruise missile and 50 million dollars for its warhead, and continued W93 and W87-1 funding; it predates enactment, is an advocacy summary used as a lead only, and the enacted law's public law number and text were not confirmed (congress.gov and the govinfo listing could not be read). Arms Control Today (September 2026, day not given) reports officials saying Los Alamos output could be accelerated by 2028 and an internal review of pit plans requested in the FY2026 appropriations act. Much of the two-site posture and warhead work predates 2025-01-20 and continues; the record reports alignment, not new causation. Overlaps the DoD-chapter record c04-06 on pits and the cruise missile.
